lead: Fresno is hot, dry and full of homes built in the 1960s to 1980s. Slab leaks, failing water heaters and roof coolers cause most of its water damage, not floods.
risk: slab leaks, aging plumbing and leaking roof coolers
risk_short: slab leaks, old pipes, roof coolers
why: About half of Fresno homes were built before 1980. Many sit on concrete slabs with copper or galvanized pipe run underneath. Years of heat, ground movement and mineral-heavy well water wear those lines down. A slab leak can run for weeks, warming the floor and soaking carpet pad before anyone notices. Swollen baseboards and a musty smell are common first signs.

Fresno only finished putting water meters on every home in December 2012. Before that, most homes paid a flat rate, so a hidden leak never showed up on a bill. Today the meters help catch leaks sooner. Summer heat brings another risk. Many homes still run evaporative coolers on the roof, and a stuck float or cracked pan can drip into the attic and stain ceilings.
image_alt: Rusted pipe dripping water above a lawn
image_caption: In Fresno, hidden slab and supply line leaks cause more water damage than storms.
problems: 1960s to 1980s homes in Sunnyside, Fig Garden
Pre-1970 homes in the Tower District
tips: Check your smart meter reading with all taps off to spot hidden leaks.
Service a roof evaporative cooler each spring and drain it in fall.
Flush the water heater once a year to clear sediment.
Feel for warm spots on floors; they can point to a slab leak.
areas: Calls come from the Tower District, Fig Garden, Sunnyside, Woodward Park, Downtown, McLane, Bullard and Roosevelt, plus Clovis, Madera and Sanger.

faq.q: How can I tell if my Fresno home has a slab leak?
faq.a: Common signs are a warm spot on the floor, the sound of running water with taps off, damp carpet or swollen baseboards, and a meter that keeps moving when nothing is on. A plumber can confirm it with pressure and acoustic tests. DryFlare then dries the floor and walls.
